title: One POST with no sign-in, 20 MB, crashes the server: zod makes one error object per array element
what_happens: POST /api/i18n with {"lang":"ta","texts":[0,0,0,...]} and 10 million numbers, no cookie. After 16 s the connection reset and the server was gone: FATAL ERROR, JavaScript heap out of memory, and the next request was refused. 4 million numbers (8 MB) took 4.8 s and 1.9 GB and it lived. The test server has the launcher's 2,048 MB heap cap. host-server.bat has no cap (the default here is 4,288 MB), so by scale a body of about 45 MB should do the same; that size was not measured. The zod rule's .max(80) does not stop it, because zod still checks every element. docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md calls this advisory (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5) 'Barely' relevant because bodies are 'already size-limited'; no size limit exists on this route. It is the only route with z.array and no session check in a simple search of src/app/api (the other 7 route files with z.array need a sign-in).
what_should_happen: An oversized request is refused before it is parsed and the server stays up. Ready patch for src/app/api/i18n/route.ts, which does not touch the owner's sign-in decision: read `const raw = await req.text();`, answer 413 when raw.length > 64_000, JSON.parse it in a try, and answer 400 when texts is not an array of at most 80 before calling Body.safeParse. Moving zod to 4.6.6 or later is the advisory's fix but is a major upgrade.
repro: node tests/qa/pass4/server.mjs start --port 3977 --instance scans-3977; node tests/qa/pass4/scan-runtime.mjs --port 3977 --zod 200000,1000000,4000000,10000000. Fast cause test: npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/scan-findings.test.ts (SCAN-1, 300,001 issues from 0.6 MB).
class: denial of service: unbounded input, no sign-in

title: next 14.2.35 has an unauthenticated remote code execution advisory for Windows hosts, and this site is hosted on Windows behind a public link
what_happens: npm audit and OSV-Scanner both list GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36, critical, with no known workaround. host-server.bat runs the site with next start on this Windows PC, and host-tunnel.bat forwards public traffic to it. docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md counts binding to 127.0.0.1 as the mitigation, but that only stops the local network: the tunnel connects from 127.0.0.1, so it does nothing while the public link is up. This finding rests on the advisory and on how the site is hosted. It was NOT exploited or tested: no exploit was tried.
what_should_happen: The server runs a fixed Next. next@15.5.24 or later fixes this one; next@15.5.28 clears all 25 next advisories by OSV's fixed versions and its peer range still takes React 18, so it looks like the smaller step, but neither version was built here. next@16.4.5 also clears the postcss advisories. Until then, keep the public link down when it is not needed. The docs call a major upgrade the owner's decision, so this is reported rather than changed.
repro: npm audit --omit=dev --json; osv-scanner scan source --format json --lockfile package-lock.json; read host-server.bat and host-tunnel.bat
class: vulnerable dependency, reachable by the advisory's terms, not reproduced

title: MySQL on this PC listens on every network address with a firewall rule open to anyone, and .env's database sign-in is the built-in admin account with a very short password
what_happens: netstat shows mysqld.exe on 0.0.0.0:3306 and [::]:3306. The enabled inbound firewall rule named Port 3306 allows TCP from any address on the Domain, Private and Public profiles. .env's DB_USER is the server's built-in admin account and DB_PASSWORD is very short (checked in code, values not printed), and DB_HOST is a loopback name, so the app does not need network access. The root .gitignore says the local MySQL holds accounts and complaints. NOT tested: nothing connected to it, so whether that password opens this server is unknown, and it was not tried from another machine. That is why this is P1 and not P0. It is machine setup, not a file in the repo; nothing was changed.
what_should_happen: The database answers only this PC, with a long random password and not the admin account. For the owner to do: set bind-address=127.0.0.1 in the server's my.ini, disable the firewall rule Port 3306 (and Port 33060 if not needed), change the password, and update .env.
repro: netstat -ano | findstr :3306; netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name="Port 3306" verbose
root_cause_guess: the PC's MySQL service settings and Windows Firewall rule, outside the repo

title: Other next advisories cannot all be ruled out, and docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md's 'No' for the WebSocket one is wrong
what_happens: GHSA-c4j6-fc7j-m34r: the audit says 'No: no WebSocket server', but the built-in server handles upgrades whatever the app does. A raw upgrade request with an absolute address made the real build run its proxy code: the log says 'Failed to proxy http:/127.0.0.1:56513/absolute', then connect refused on port 80 of this PC. Choosing the target was NOT shown: my listener was never called in 5 request forms, because Next squeezes the // out of the address. So what was shown is the server trying port 80 on itself, on a direct connection. Whether that gets through a public tunnel was not tested. GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf, GHSA-q4gf-8mx6-v5v3 and GHSA-8h8q-6873-q5fj (denial of service on App Router server functions): the app has no server actions, but this was not tested with a crafted request, so they stay open. Image optimizer, Server Actions, Pages Router and rewrite advisories were checked and do not apply (triage.json).
what_should_happen: The same upgrade as SCAN-2 closes them. Correct the row in docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md.
repro: node tests/qa/pass4/scan-runtime.mjs --port 3977, then look at upgrade in the output and 'Failed to proxy' in data/aws-cache/qa/run/srv-3977.log
root_cause_guess: node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-server.js:486 (proxies an upgrade whenever the parsed URL has a protocol)
class: vulnerable dependency; wrong claim in a security document

title: A production build never shows a reset code, but a dev server with this .env gives one to anyone, and the tunnel does not check which server it is forwarding
what_happens: Production is clean: in .next-qa the helper compiled to an empty function, the flag's name is nowhere in the build, and a real reset request returned no code while the cooldown on the second request proved a code was made. The gap: .env turns NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_SHOW_OTP on, and .env.aws.example:23 tells teammates to do the same. Under npm run dev the route returns the code in JSON for any registered email with no sign-in (documented in the README). start.bat runs that dev server on port 3000, the same port host-tunnel.bat forwards. If start.bat is running when the tunnel opens, anyone on the internet could read a reset code for any account and take it over. That needs someone to start the wrong script; it is not happening now. The dev branch is shown by a unit test; a real next dev run was not done because the shared machine was short of memory.
what_should_happen: A code is never sent to a request from outside this PC, even in dev. Ready patch that leaves host-server.bat and host-tunnel.bat alone: pass the request to devOtpForResponse and also return undefined unless the Host header is 127.0.0.1 or localhost and there is no x-forwarded-for header. Consider false in .env.aws.example.
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/scan-findings.test.ts (the production branch, the dev branch and the compiled route); node tests/qa/pass4/scan-runtime.mjs --port 3977 (real production run)
class: unsafe default in a dev path that can reach production traffic

title: AES-GCM decryption does not fix the tag length, so a 4-byte tag is accepted
what_happens: Semgrep's gcm-no-tag-length on src/lib/crypto.ts:23 is real: an iv plus a 4-byte tag decrypts to an empty string with no error, and Node logs deprecation DEP0182. The harm is small: it needs write access to the stored value, a tag can only be short when there is no message, and the result is empty.
what_should_happen: Short tags are refused. Patch: crypto.createDecipheriv("aes-256-gcm", KEY(), iv, { authTagLength: 16 }).

title: A malformed body on the mobile code request crashes the handler with a 500, though the line's own comment promises a 400
what_happens: POST /api/profile/mobile-otp/request, signed in, body {not json: 500, and the server log shows TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'mobileNumber'). A sign-in is needed and nothing is damaged.
what_should_happen: A 400 from the schema. Patch: body?.mobileNumber on line 16.
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/scan-findings.test.ts (SCAN-6); node tests/qa/pass4/scan-runtime.mjs --port 3977 (malformedBodyOnMobileOtp)

title: Production accepts the JWT_SECRET placeholder from the public .env.example
what_happens: src/lib/secrets.ts only checks the length (32 bytes or more). The placeholder in .env.example is longer than that, so a server started from a plain copy of that file runs, and its token key is printed in a public repo: anyone could forge a Collector's token. This is not happening today: .env has a different value of its own, and DEPLOYMENT.md:55 says to generate one. .env.aws.example's placeholder is under 32 bytes and is refused already.
what_should_happen: The server refuses to start on a known placeholder, like it refuses a short one. Patch in strongSecret: also throw WeakSecretError in production when the value contains a placeholder word such as change or your, or equals the .env.example text.
